investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-20T01:04 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check with the same error message and zero evidence was collected, the root cause is localized to the swarm gateway layer, not to individual eval logic or the production API application tier.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every call to POST /api/agents returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", preventing agent creation from starting and leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) completely absent. The failure is scoped to this eval run and the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=748, max=300)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 748 minutes old, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all sibling public-website checks passed, and there is no evidence of a user-facing outage.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 748 minutes (approximately 12.5 hours). The contract requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 (5 hours). The snapshot itself is structurally valid and sourced from github-actions, meaning the workflow ran at some point but has since stalled, been skipped, or failed silently without updating the published file. This is an eval-layer staleness failure, not a public website outage.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=748, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot is reachable and structurally valid but stale by 448 minutes beyond the allowed threshold.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the exact contract boundary that was crossed.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 and valid app shells — confirms the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness, not general site availability.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot has not executed successfully within the last 748+ minutes. The workflow may have been skipped, cancelled, or failed without publishing a new snapshot file.
The scheduled trigger for the snapshot-publishing workflow was disabled, removed, or its cron schedule was altered such that it no longer fires at the expected cadence.
The workflow ran but failed during the publish/push step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deployment error or permissions issue), leaving the previously published snapshot in place with an old timestamp.
A GitHub Actions quota, rate limit, or runner availability issue prevented the workflow from completing in the expected window.

The snapshotUrl (https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json) is serving a cached or CDN-stale version of the file even though a newer file was published — though this is less likely given the magnitude of the age gap (748 minutes).

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale GitHub Actions Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=748, max=300)
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json is 748 minutes old, exceeding the contract maximum of 300 minutes. This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness assertion; all sibling public-website checks passed, and there is no evidence of a user-facing outage.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 748 minutes (approximately 12.5 hours). The contract requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 (5 hours). The snapshot itself is structurally valid and sourced from github-actions, meaning the workflow ran at some point but has since stalled, been skipped, or failed silently without updating the published file. This is an eval-layer staleness failure, not a public website outage.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=748, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot is reachable and structurally valid but stale by 448 minutes beyond the allowed threshold.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the exact contract boundary that was crossed.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 and valid app shells — confirms the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness, not general site availability.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot has not executed successfully within the last 748+ minutes. The workflow may have been skipped, cancelled, or failed without publishing a new snapshot file.
The scheduled trigger for the snapshot-publishing workflow was disabled, removed, or its cron schedule was altered such that it no longer fires at the expected cadence.
The workflow ran but failed during the publish/push step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deployment error or permissions issue), leaving the previously published snapshot in place with an old timestamp.
A GitHub Actions quota, rate limit, or runner availability issue prevented the workflow from completing in the expected window.

The snapshotUrl (https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json) is serving a cached or CDN-stale version of the file even though a newer file was published — though this is less likely given the magnitude of the age gap (748 minutes).
